references.text: Describes the righteous as a tree planted by flowing water, similar to the image of trees by streams in Balaam's prophecy.
Uses the image of a well-watered garden as a symbol of blessing and fertility, corresponding to Balaam's description of Israel as gardens by a river.
Compares the blessed one to a well-watered garden, similar to Balaam's image of Israel's fertility.
Describes cedar trees by water as an image of greatness and growth, corresponding to the cedars by water in Balaam's prophecy.
Refers to the Lord's trees and the cedars of Lebanon that He has planted, similar to the image of the Lord planting aloes.
Describes the river as the water of Eden's garden, a fundamental symbol of fertility that echoes in Balaam's prophecy.
The promise that Israel's descendants will grow up like grass by streams of water and like willows by flowing water.
